project.name: manifold
project.description: Generic adapter implementations for Converge contracts. A Converge extension providing vendor-agnostic adapters for LLM, search, fetch, feed, storage, vector, experience, embedding, reranking, and tool backends.

nodes.name: openrouter.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the OpenRouter multi-provider aggregator adapter with optional site metadata headers, detailed per-provider cost extraction from native usage fields, and retry logic.

nodes.name: perplexity.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the Perplexity AI chat backend adapter, handling search-grounded responses with citation metadata extraction on top of an OpenAI-compatible API.

nodes.name: qwen.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the Alibaba Qwen chat backend adapter (OpenAI-compatible) with full request/response mapping, retry logic, and tool call support.

nodes.name: resilient.rs
nodes.summary: Implements a resilient chat backend that wraps a primary ChatBackend with an ordered list of fallbacks, retrying on format-contract failures and model-missing errors with alternative configurations.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses trait objects (Box<dyn ChatBackend>) to compose arbitrary backend chains without generics, enabling runtime fallback selection.

nodes.name: retry.rs
nodes.summary: Provides exponential-backoff retry infrastructure used by all LLM backend adapters, exposing a typed RetryOutcome enum to distinguish retry, abort, and success results.

nodes.name: staik.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the Staik AI chat backend adapter with OpenAI-compatible request/response mapping, tool call support, bearer-token auth, and retry logic.

nodes.name: streaming.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the ChatEvent enum for server-sent event streaming and the StreamingChatBackend trait for LLM adapters that support token-by-token output.

nodes.name: writer.rs
nodes.summary: Thin adapter wrapping Writer.com's LLM service as a Converge ChatBackend, delegating to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint with secret-based API key resolution.

nodes.name: gcp.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the GCP Secret Manager secret provider, fetching API keys via the GCP metadata server for access tokens and the Secret Manager REST API with base64 decoding.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the GCP metadata server (169.254.169.254) for workload-identity token retrieval, avoiding the need for service-account JSON files.

nodes.name: keychain.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the macOS Keychain secret provider using the security CLI to read API keys from named Keychain services on developer machines.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Core secret management module defining the SecretProvider trait, SecretString zeroizing wrapper, and multiple provider implementations including env-var, default chain, and static in-memory providers.
nodes.languageNotes: SecretString implements Drop to zero memory on release and Debug to redact the value, preventing accidental secret exposure in logs.

nodes.name: names.rs
nodes.summary: Maps logical secret key names to provider-specific aliases, macOS Keychain service names, and GCP short names for consistent multi-backend secret resolution.

nodes.name: PerplexityBackend

nodes.name: QwenBackend

nodes.name: ResilientChatBackend

nodes.name: RetryOutcome
nodes.summary: Typed enum representing the three possible outcomes of a retried operation: success, retryable failure with delay, or terminal abort.

nodes.name: StaikBackend

nodes.name: SecretError

nodes.name: SecretString

nodes.name: call_local
nodes.summary: Sends embedding requests to a locally hosted HTTP endpoint (e.g., Ollama or vLLM-compatible server) and parses the response.

nodes.name: embed
nodes.summary: Entry point for the embedding contract: dispatches the request to the configured backend endpoint and returns normalized embedding vectors.

nodes.name: input_to_content
nodes.summary: Converts generic EmbedInput items (text, image URLs, etc.) into the backend-specific InputContent format required by Qwen-VL API endpoints.

nodes.name: ScraperHtmlBackend
nodes.summary: Default HtmlExtractBackend implementation using the scraper crate for CSS-selector-based HTML parsing and content node extraction.

nodes.name: HtmlExtractBackend
nodes.summary: Trait defining the HTML extraction contract, with methods for extracting structured content nodes from raw HTML bytes.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Parses HTML bytes using the scraper crate, selects semantic content elements, and returns a list of ExtractedNode items representing the document's main content.

nodes.name: HttpFeedProvider
nodes.summary: Concrete FeedFetchBackend implementation that probes, fetches, and parses RSS/Atom/JSON feeds over HTTP, delegating URL validation to the fetch layer.

nodes.name: FeedFetchBackend
nodes.summary: Trait defining the feed fetch contract, with probe and fetch methods separating feed discovery from content retrieval.

nodes.name: parse_xml_feed
nodes.summary: Parses RSS and Atom XML byte streams into a list of FeedItem values using a streaming XML reader, supporting both format variants.

nodes.name: discover_alternate_links
nodes.summary: Scans an HTML document for link[rel=alternate] elements pointing to RSS/Atom feeds and returns a list of candidate feed URLs with detected format hints.

nodes.name: parse_json_feed
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON Feed (version 1.x) byte stream into a list of FeedItem values, normalizing authors, content, and dates.

nodes.name: probe
nodes.summary: Probes a URL to determine whether it is a feed or an HTML page, returning a FeedProbeResponse that either confirms the feed format or lists alternate feed candidates discovered via link headers or HTML parsing.

nodes.name: HttpFetchProvider
nodes.summary: WebFetchBackend implementation that performs hardened HTTP GET/POST requests with SSRF protection, redirect validation, and configurable byte-limit enforcement.

nodes.name: fetch
nodes.summary: Core fetch implementation: validates the request URL, issues the HTTP request with per-caller headers, follows redirects with safety checks, reads a bounded body, and returns a WebFetchResponse.

nodes.name: validate_outbound_url
nodes.summary: Validates that an outbound URL uses an allowed scheme and does not resolve to a private/loopback IP address, protecting against SSRF attacks.

nodes.name: config.rs
nodes.summary: YAML-driven configuration loader that parses a `ToolsConfig` struct and assembles a `ToolRegistry` from OpenAPI specs, GraphQL endpoints, and inline tool definitions.

nodes.name: ToolsConfigError
nodes.summary: Error enum for configuration loading failures, covering I/O errors, YAML parse failures, validation issues, and downstream tool errors.

nodes.name: ToolsConfig
nodes.summary: Top-level YAML configuration struct holding arrays of OpenAPI spec configs, GraphQL endpoint configs, and inline tool definitions.

nodes.name: OpenApiConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for a single OpenAPI spec source, holding the file path, base URL, optional name prefix, tag filters, and enabled flag, with methods to construct a converter and load tools.

nodes.name: GraphQlConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for a GraphQL endpoint source, specifying the endpoint URL, auth header, operation type flags, name prefix, and field filters, with a method to construct a converter.

nodes.name: InlineToolConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for a statically defined inline tool with a name, description, JSON Schema input, and enabled flag, with a method to produce a `ToolDefinition`.

nodes.name: OpenApiConfig::to_converter
nodes.summary: Constructs an `OpenApiConverter` from this config, applying base URL, name prefix, and tag filter options.

nodes.name: GraphQlConfig::to_converter
nodes.summary: Constructs a `GraphQlConverter` from this config, applying endpoint, operation type flags, name prefix, and field filter options.

nodes.name: build_registry_from_config
nodes.summary: Builds a `ToolRegistry` from a `ToolsConfig` by loading OpenAPI specs, connecting GraphQL endpoints, and registering inline tools — the primary composition entry point for config-driven tool setup.

nodes.name: definition.rs
nodes.summary: Core type definitions for the tool abstraction layer: `ToolDefinition`, `InputSchema`, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, and their associated source provenance and content enums.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an atomic counter combined with a millisecond timestamp to generate unique tool call IDs without external dependencies.

nodes.name: ToolDefinition
nodes.summary: Represents a callable tool with a name, description, JSON Schema input, optional source provenance (MCP/OpenAPI/GraphQL/Inline), and arbitrary string annotations.

nodes.name: ToolSource
nodes.summary: Enum encoding the origin of a tool — MCP server, OpenAPI spec operation, GraphQL operation, or inline definition — each carrying source-specific metadata.

nodes.name: GraphQlOperationType
nodes.summary: Enum distinguishing the three GraphQL operation types (Query, Mutation, Subscription) carried in `ToolSource::GraphQl` variants.

nodes.name: InputSchema
nodes.summary: Wraps a raw JSON Schema value and provides helpers to construct an empty schema, extract required property names, and access top-level property definitions.

nodes.name: ToolCall
nodes.summary: Represents an LLM-initiated tool invocation with an auto-generated call ID, tool name, and JSON arguments map.

nodes.name: ToolResult
nodes.summary: Represents the outcome of a tool execution, carrying the call ID, text or JSON content, an error flag, and an extensible metadata map.

nodes.name: ToolResultContent
nodes.summary: Enum for tool result content variants: plain text (`Text`) or structured JSON (`Json`).

nodes.name: InputSchema::required_properties
nodes.summary: Extracts the list of required property names from the JSON Schema's `required` array, returning an empty vector when the field is absent.

nodes.name: generate_call_id
nodes.summary: Generates a unique tool call ID by combining a millisecond timestamp with a process-global atomic counter, ensuring monotonic uniqueness without external dependencies.

nodes.name: error.rs
nodes.summary: Error types for the tool subsystem: defines `ToolErrorKind` variants and the `ToolError` struct with ergonomic constructor helpers and retryability detection.

nodes.name: ToolErrorKind
nodes.summary: Enum of tool error categories — not-found, invalid arguments, execution failure, connection failure, server error, timeout, validation failure, permission denial, and unsupported source — with retryability classification.

nodes.name: ToolError
nodes.summary: Structured tool error carrying a `ToolErrorKind`, human-readable message, and optional source chain, with factory methods for common error scenarios and retryability detection.

nodes.name: graphql.rs
nodes.summary: GraphQL introspection-to-tool converter: parses introspection JSON, maps query and mutation fields to `ToolDefinition` instances with recursively derived JSON Schema input schemas.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses recursive type-ref resolution to handle NON_NULL and LIST wrappers in GraphQL type references when generating JSON Schema fragments.

nodes.name: GraphQlConverter
nodes.summary: Configurable converter from GraphQL introspection JSON to a list of `ToolDefinition`s, with options for filtering by operation type, field name substrings, and adding a name prefix.

nodes.name: GraphQlIntrospectionResult
nodes.summary: Deserializable wrapper for the top-level GraphQL introspection response envelope containing a `data` field.

nodes.name: GraphQlIntrospectionData
nodes.summary: Deserializable container for the `data.__schema` field from a GraphQL introspection response.

nodes.name: GraphQlSchema
nodes.summary: Deserializable representation of the GraphQL `__Schema` type, carrying query type, mutation type, and the full list of defined types.

nodes.name: GraphQlType
nodes.summary: Deserializable GraphQL type definition with kind, name, description, fields, and input fields for introspection parsing.

nodes.name: GraphQlField
nodes.summary: Deserializable GraphQL field with name, description, and argument list for introspection-based tool generation.

nodes.name: GraphQlInputValue
nodes.summary: Deserializable GraphQL input value (operation argument) with name, description, and type reference for JSON Schema mapping.

nodes.name: GraphQlTypeRef
nodes.summary: Deserializable recursive GraphQL type reference encoding NON_NULL, LIST, and NAMED variants for translation to JSON Schema fragments.

nodes.name: GraphQlConverter::convert_schema
nodes.summary: Converts a parsed `GraphQlIntrospectionResult` to a list of `ToolDefinition`s by resolving the query and mutation root types from the type map and delegating field conversion.

nodes.name: GraphQlConverter::convert_type_fields
nodes.summary: Maps the fields of a GraphQL object type to `ToolDefinition`s, applying field name filters, name prefix, and building per-field input schemas.

nodes.name: GraphQlConverter::build_input_schema
nodes.summary: Converts the argument list of a GraphQL field to a JSON Schema `InputSchema`, classifying arguments as required or optional based on NON_NULL wrapping.

nodes.name: GraphQlConverter::type_ref_to_schema
nodes.summary: Recursively translates a `GraphQlTypeRef` (NON_NULL, LIST, or NAMED) to a JSON Schema fragment used when constructing `InputSchema` for GraphQL arguments.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for the tools subsystem that declares all sub-modules and defines the `ToolFormat` enum for controlling LLM tool serialization format.

nodes.name: ToolFormat
nodes.summary: Enum selecting the serialization format for tool definitions when calling LLMs: Anthropic native format, OpenAI function-calling format, or Generic JSON.

nodes.name: openapi.rs
nodes.summary: OpenAPI 3.x spec-to-tool converter: parses YAML or JSON specs and maps each HTTP operation to a `ToolDefinition` with JSON Schema input schemas derived from path parameters, query parameters, and request bodies.

nodes.name: OpenApiConverter
nodes.summary: Configurable converter from OpenAPI 3.x specs (YAML or JSON) to `ToolDefinition` lists, with support for base URL override, tag filtering, and name prefixing.

nodes.name: OpenApiSpec
nodes.summary: Deserializable OpenAPI 3.x root object with version string, info block, server list, and paths map.

nodes.name: OpenApiInfo
nodes.summary: Deserializable OpenAPI info block carrying title and version strings.

nodes.name: OpenApiServer
nodes.summary: Deserializable OpenAPI server object holding the base URL string.

nodes.name: OpenApiPathItem
nodes.summary: Deserializable OpenAPI path item holding optional operations for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE HTTP methods.

nodes.name: OpenApiOperation
nodes.summary: Deserializable OpenAPI operation object with operation ID, summary, description, tags, parameters, and request body.

nodes.name: OpenApiParameter
nodes.summary: Deserializable OpenAPI parameter with name, location (path/query/header/cookie), required flag, and JSON Schema.

nodes.name: OpenApiRequestBody
nodes.summary: Deserializable OpenAPI request body holding a content map keyed by media type string.

nodes.name: OpenApiMediaType
nodes.summary: Deserializable OpenAPI media type object holding an optional JSON Schema value.

nodes.name: OpenApiConverter::convert_spec
nodes.summary: Iterates all paths and HTTP methods in a parsed OpenAPI spec, applying tag and name-prefix filters to produce a `ToolDefinition` per operation with base-URL and HTTP method annotations.

nodes.name: OpenApiConverter::build_input_schema
nodes.summary: Builds an `InputSchema` for an OpenAPI operation by merging path-template parameters, explicit query/header parameters, and request body JSON Schema properties into a unified schema.

nodes.name: registry.rs
nodes.summary: In-memory tool registry that stores, retrieves, and routes `ToolDefinition`s by name and source type, with serialization helpers for Anthropic and generic OpenAI LLM formats.

nodes.name: ToolRegistry
nodes.summary: Central in-memory store for `ToolDefinition`s indexed by name, providing registration, lookup, source-based filtering, and serialization to Anthropic and generic LLM tool formats.

nodes.name: SourceFilter
nodes.summary: Enum for filtering tools in `ToolRegistry` by their origin: All, MCP, OpenAPI, GraphQL, or Inline, with a `matches` method for predicate use.

nodes.name: ToolHandler
nodes.summary: Trait defining the contract for tool execution backends: `can_handle` checks whether a tool is supported and `execute` runs the tool call asynchronously.

nodes.name: ToolRegistry::call_tool
nodes.summary: Dispatches a `ToolCall` by looking up the tool definition and returning an `UnsupportedSource` error for source types (MCP, GraphQL, OpenAPI, Inline) that require external handlers.

nodes.name: ToolRegistry::to_llm_tools
nodes.summary: Serializes all registered tools to the OpenAI/generic LLM function-calling JSON format with `type: 'function'` and `function.parameters`.

nodes.name: ToolRegistry::to_anthropic_tools
nodes.summary: Serializes all registered tools to Anthropic's tool format with `name`, `description`, and `input_schema` fields for use in Claude API calls.

nodes.name: cost_routing.rs
nodes.summary: Provides cost-aware model routing via a `CostBudget` struct that estimates per-call USD cost and filters candidate models against a configurable budget ceiling, with both lenient and strict modes for handling unpriced models.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses builder-pattern setters (`strict()`) on `CostBudget` to flip the budget enforcement mode after construction.

nodes.name: fuzzy_fitness.rs
nodes.summary: Implements a fuzzy-logic inference engine (variables and rules cached in `OnceLock`) to compute a dimensionless preference score for each LLM candidate based on cost, latency, and quality inputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Fuzzy variables and rules are lazily initialized via `OnceLock` for zero-cost reuse across repeated scoring calls without synchronization overhead.

nodes.name: selection.rs
nodes.summary: Resolves and instantiates the best chat backend for a given `ChatBackendSelectionConfig` by querying the model registry, filtering by available secrets, and dispatching to vendor-specific adapters (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, and nine other providers).
nodes.languageNotes: Provider availability is probed at selection time by checking secret presence; the healthy-backend variant additionally fires a probe request to exclude backends that are reachable but misbehaving.

nodes.name: model_selection.rs
nodes.summary: Core model-selection infrastructure: `ModelMetadata` encodes the per-model capability matrix, `ModelSelector` ranks candidates by fuzzy fitness score, and `ProviderRegistry` gates selection on live credential detection via environment secrets.
nodes.languageNotes: Provider availability checking can be bypassed via an atomic `SKIP_AVAILABILITY_CHECK` flag used in tests to avoid requiring real API keys.

nodes.name: registry_loader.rs
nodes.summary: Parses the YAML model registry file (or embedded default YAML) into typed `LoadedRegistry`/`LoadedProvider`/`LoadedModel` domain objects and converts them to a `ModelSelector` ready for capability-based querying.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on all YAML structs to surface schema drift as hard validation errors rather than silently ignoring new fields.

nodes.name: CostBudget
nodes.summary: Encodes a per-call USD cost budget using prompt-token estimate, max completion tokens, and a ceiling price; evaluates whether a candidate model's pricing fits within the budget and returns structured rejection reasons when it does not.

nodes.name: FitnessSummary
nodes.summary: Snapshot of fuzzy inference outputs for a candidate model, holding membership degrees for the preference, cost-cheapness, latency-fastness, and quality-highness variables plus the IDs of activated rules.

nodes.name: SelectedChatBackend
nodes.summary: Bundles a resolved `Arc<dyn ChatBackend>` with the `SelectionResult` that chose it, exposing `provider()` and `model()` accessors for downstream routing decisions.

nodes.name: FitnessBreakdown
nodes.summary: Granular fitness decomposition for a model candidate, exposing per-axis cost, latency, and quality scores plus a weighted total used to rank candidates during selection.

nodes.name: SelectionResult
nodes.summary: Full selection outcome including the chosen model metadata, its fitness breakdown, all considered candidate models with scores, and the list of models rejected with their reasons.

nodes.name: RejectionReason
nodes.summary: Exhaustive enum of reasons a model was excluded from selection, covering cost class, latency, quality, capability flags (reasoning, web search, tool use, vision, context window, structured output, code, multilingual), data-sovereignty, compliance, and budget mismatches.

nodes.name: ModelMetadata
nodes.summary: Complete capability matrix for a single LLM model, encoding provider identity, cost/latency/quality scalars, capability flags, data-sovereignty, compliance, optional pricing, and an OpenRouter routing ID; evaluates `satisfies`, computes fuzzy fitness scores, and explains rejections against `AgentRequirements`.
nodes.languageNotes: Builder-pattern `with_*` setters return `Self` for ergonomic chaining; quality is clamped to [0.0, 1.0] in `new()`.

nodes.name: ModelSelector
nodes.summary: In-memory roster of `ModelMetadata` entries that filters and ranks candidates against `AgentRequirements` using fuzzy fitness scores, returning the best-scoring model as a provider/model name pair.

nodes.name: ProviderRegistry
nodes.summary: Provider-availability-aware wrapper around `ModelSelector` that gates candidate models on live credential detection in environment variables; supports catalog-based metadata overrides and produces detailed `SelectionResult` with per-model rejection reasons.

nodes.name: RegistryError
nodes.summary: Error enum for YAML registry loading, distinguishing filesystem I/O failures, YAML parse errors, and schema-validation errors (missing fields, out-of-range values, etc.).

nodes.name: LoadedProvider
nodes.summary: Deserialized and validated provider entry from the registry YAML holding auth config (env key, secondary key, key URL, API URL), geographic/compliance metadata, and a list of `LoadedModel` entries; `is_available()` probes the environment for the configured API key.

nodes.name: LoadedModel
nodes.summary: Richly-typed deserialized model entry holding cost class, latency, quality, capability flags, modalities, architecture, agentic settings, pricing, rate limits, and benchmark/provenance metadata after YAML parse and validation.

nodes.name: LoadedRegistry
nodes.summary: Root container for all loaded providers with convenience accessors for filtering by model type (LLM, embedding, reranker) and converting the registry into a `ModelSelector` for capability-based querying.

nodes.name: select_within_budget
nodes.summary: Runs a full model selection pass and then filters the ranked candidates by `CostBudget.admits()`, returning the first in-budget model or an error that names each over-budget candidate with its rejection reason.

nodes.name: list_within_budget
nodes.summary: Returns all models satisfying the given requirements whose estimated call cost falls within the provided `CostBudget`.

nodes.name: rejection_reason
nodes.summary: Returns a human-readable rejection message if the model's estimated cost exceeds the budget, or if strict mode rejects an unpriced model; returns `None` when the model is admitted.

nodes.name: fuzzy_fitness
nodes.summary: Runs the fuzzy inference engine on cost, latency, and quality scalars derived from `ModelMetadata`, returning the raw inference output or `None` when inference produces no activated rules.

nodes.name: fitness_summary
nodes.summary: Wraps `fuzzy_fitness` to return a `FitnessSummary` with weighted preference score and membership degrees for each input variable, defaulting to zero when inference fails.

nodes.name: build_variables
nodes.summary: Constructs the full set of fuzzy linguistic variables (cost, latency, quality, preference) with trapezoid and triangle membership functions defining the cheap/moderate/expensive, fast/medium/slow, low/medium/high, and weak/moderate/strong fuzzy sets.

nodes.name: build_rules
nodes.summary: Defines the fuzzy inference rule base mapping cost/latency/quality conjunctions to preference output sets (e.g., cheap AND high-quality → strong preference; expensive AND slow → weak preference).

nodes.name: weighted_preference
nodes.summary: Converts the fuzzy output memberships for the weak/moderate/strong preference sets into a single scalar by computing a weighted centroid (0.2 × weak + 0.6 × moderate + 1.0 × strong).

nodes.name: cost_proxy_usd_per_million
nodes.summary: Converts a model's pricing or cost class into a USD-per-million-token proxy value used as the cost input to the fuzzy inference engine.

nodes.name: select_chat_backend_with_secret_provider
nodes.summary: Builds a model registry for the given config and secret provider, runs capability-aware selection, then resolves the winning model to a live backend instance, returning a `SelectedChatBackend`.

nodes.name: select_healthy_chat_backend_with_secret_provider
nodes.summary: Like `select_chat_backend_with_secret_provider` but iterates candidates in fitness order, firing a lightweight probe request to each until one responds successfully, falling back to the next candidate on failure.

nodes.name: instantiate_backend_for_model
nodes.summary: Dispatches on `ModelMetadata.provider` to construct the matching vendor backend (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, OpenRouter, Kong, Staik, Arcee, Writer, MinMax, DeepSeek, Kimi, Perplexity, Qwen) using credentials from the secret provider.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a `match` arm per provider string; adding a new vendor requires registering it in this match, in `chat_provider_registry`, `is_chat_provider_available`, and `normalize_provider_name`.

nodes.name: model_registry_for_config
nodes.summary: Builds a `ProviderRegistry` appropriate for the selection config: when a provider override is set it validates the name and verifies credentials; otherwise it enumerates all available providers from the environment.

nodes.name: is_chat_provider_available
nodes.summary: Returns `true` if the given provider name has its required API key secret present; Kong additionally requires a `KONG_AI_GATEWAY_URL` environment variable.

nodes.name: satisfies
nodes.summary: Evaluates all `AgentRequirements` dimensions (cost class, latency, quality, capability flags, data-sovereignty, compliance, context window) against `ModelMetadata` fields and returns `true` only if every constraint is met.

nodes.name: rejection_reason
nodes.summary: Returns the first `RejectionReason` that explains why a model fails a given `AgentRequirements`, checking each constraint in priority order; returns `None` when the model fully satisfies the requirements.

nodes.name: select_with_details
nodes.summary: Iterates all models in the registry, separates them into candidates (with fitness breakdowns) and rejected (with reasons), sorts candidates by total fitness score, and returns the top model in a `SelectionResult`.

nodes.name: from_env
nodes.summary: Initializes `ProviderRegistry` by loading all known providers, filtering to those with credentials present in the environment, and setting up an empty metadata-overrides map.

nodes.name: is_provider_available
nodes.summary: Checks whether a named provider's credentials are present in the environment secrets, returning `false` for unknown providers; short-circuits to `true` when the test availability-check bypass flag is set.

nodes.name: load_registry_from_str
nodes.summary: Parses a YAML string into `RegistryYaml`, validates every provider and model entry, converts YAML enums to domain types (capabilities, modalities, compliance), and assembles a `LoadedRegistry`; returns a `ValidationError` collecting all failures.

nodes.name: load_registry
nodes.summary: Loads the model registry from an env-overridable path, falling back through the default file path and a crate-local path before falling back to the embedded YAML constant.

nodes.name: validate_provider
nodes.summary: Validates a `ProviderYaml` entry: checks that `env_key` is non-empty, URLs begin with `http`, country code is exactly 2 characters, and the model list is non-empty.

nodes.name: validate_model
nodes.summary: Validates a `ModelYaml` entry: ensures quality is in [0.0, 1.0], latency is non-zero, cost class is valid, and that embedding models specify a dimensions field.

nodes.name: to_model_selector
nodes.summary: Converts a `LoadedRegistry` into a `ModelSelector` by mapping each (provider, LLM model) pair to a `ModelMetadata` instance with full capability and geographic metadata applied.

nodes.name: gcs.rs
nodes.summary: Provides factory functions for constructing Google Cloud Storage object store instances, supporting both authenticated access (via environment credentials) and unauthenticated public bucket access.
nodes.languageNotes: build uses GoogleCloudStorageBuilder::from_env() for credential-based access; build_public adds with_skip_signature(true) for anonymous public bucket reads.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Constructs an authenticated GCS object store for a given bucket name using environment-sourced credentials.

nodes.name: build_public
nodes.summary: Constructs an unauthenticated GCS object store for public buckets by skipping request signing.

nodes.name: huggingface.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the object_store::ObjectStore trait for HuggingFace Hub datasets, supporting path parsing with username/dataset/revision segments, metadata retrieval via HTTP HEAD requests, and file downloads via the hf-hub local cache.
nodes.languageNotes: Read-only adapter: put, copy, delete, and list_with_delimiter all return NotSupported errors. get_opts checks a local hf-hub cache first before falling back to network download.

nodes.name: HuggingFaceError
nodes.summary: Error enum for HuggingFace API interactions, covering API errors, HTTP request failures, missing response headers, and invalid path formats.

nodes.name: HuggingFacePath
nodes.summary: Parses and represents a HuggingFace dataset path of the form username/dataset[@revision]/path, providing accessors for building hf-hub Repo references and matching file listings.

nodes.name: HuggingFaceObjectStore
nodes.summary: Implements the object_store::ObjectStore trait for HuggingFace Hub datasets, using an hf-hub API client for network access and a LocalFileSystem for cache-hit reads.

nodes.name: local.rs
nodes.summary: Provides a factory function that creates a LocalFileSystem object store for a given path, automatically creating the directory if it does not yet exist.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Creates a LocalFileSystem object store rooted at the given path, creating the directory with create_dir_all if it does not exist.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module entry point for the object_storage subsystem; exposes build_store, a URL-scheme-driven factory that dispatches to the local, S3, GCS, or HuggingFace backend based on the configured URI.

nodes.name: build_store
nodes.summary: Dispatches object store construction based on the URI scheme in StorageConfig, routing to local, s3, gs (public or authenticated), or returning an UnsupportedScheme error.

nodes.name: resolve_s3_options
nodes.summary: Merges S3 endpoint and region values, preferring values from StorageConfig over those embedded in the URI.

nodes.name: s3.rs
nodes.summary: Provides a factory function for constructing an Amazon S3 object store, supporting optional custom endpoint and region overrides for S3-compatible storage backends.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AmazonS3Builder::from_env() as the base, conditionally adds with_allow_http when a custom endpoint is supplied to support non-TLS S3-compatible services.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Constructs an AmazonS3 object store for a given bucket, applying optional endpoint and region overrides and enabling HTTP for non-HTTPS custom endpoints.

nodes.name: lancedb.rs
nodes.summary: Persistent vector store adapter backed by LanceDB, managing Apache Arrow-format data serialization, Tokio runtime injection or self-ownership, and full CRUD plus nearest-neighbor search against LanceDB tables. Includes comprehensive inline unit tests.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges a sync Rust interface with async LanceDB by calling `runtime.block_on()` throughout; uses Apache Arrow `RecordBatch` for columnar storage and `merge_insert` for upsert semantics.

nodes.name: LanceStore
nodes.summary: Exported persistent vector store struct backed by a LanceDB connection, holding an Arrow-schema table, a cached `RwLock<Option<Table>>`, and a Tokio runtime handle for blocking async I/O.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a `LanceStore` by connecting to a LanceDB database at the given path, spawning a new Tokio runtime if none is currently active.

nodes.name: with_runtime
nodes.summary: Alternate constructor for `LanceStore` that accepts an externally provided Tokio runtime handle, suitable for embedding within an existing async executor.

nodes.name: get_or_create_table
nodes.summary: Lazily opens or creates the LanceDB table for the configured table name, initializing it with an empty Arrow-schema batch if it does not yet exist.

nodes.name: create_arrow_schema
nodes.summary: Builds the Apache Arrow schema for the LanceDB table, defining the `id` (Utf8), `vector` (FixedSizeList<Float32>), and `payload` (Utf8 JSON) columns.

nodes.name: create_empty_batch
nodes.summary: Constructs an empty Apache Arrow `RecordBatch` conforming to the store schema, used to initialize a new LanceDB table with the correct column layout.

nodes.name: records_to_batch
nodes.summary: Converts a slice of `VectorRecord` structs into an Apache Arrow `RecordBatch`, validating vector dimensionality and serializing JSON payloads before constructing the columnar batch.

nodes.name: upsert_batch
nodes.summary: Upserts a batch of vector records into the LanceDB table using Arrow's `merge_insert` with update-or-insert semantics keyed on the `id` column.

nodes.name: query
nodes.summary: Executes a nearest-neighbor vector search against the LanceDB table, converts Arrow `RecordBatch` results into `VectorMatch` structs, sorts by descending distance score, and applies `top_k` truncation.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Removes a single vector record from the LanceDB table by its string ID using a SQL-style filter predicate.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Drops the LanceDB table entirely if it exists and resets the cached table handle to `None`, leaving the store in a clean initial state.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Returns the total number of rows in the LanceDB table via `table.count_rows`.

nodes.name: memory.rs
nodes.summary: Thread-safe in-memory vector store backed by a `RwLock<HashMap>`, implementing cosine-similarity nearest-neighbor search with optional minimum-score filtering. Includes inline unit tests covering upsert, query, overwrite, delete, and clear.

nodes.name: InMemoryVectorStore
nodes.summary: Exported in-memory vector store keyed by string ID using a `RwLock<HashMap>`, supporting upsert, cosine-similarity query with optional score threshold, delete, and clear.

nodes.name: query
nodes.summary: Scores all stored records using cosine similarity against the query vector, applies optional minimum-score filtering, sorts results descending by score, and truncates to `top_k`.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Vector submodule barrel that declares the `lancedb`, `memory`, and `qdrant` backend modules and exports shared math utilities `cosine_similarity` and `normalize` used across vector store implementations.

nodes.name: cosine_similarity
nodes.summary: Computes the cosine similarity between two f32 slices, returning 0.0 for empty or mismatched-length vectors.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Normalizes a slice of f32 values to unit length; returns the original vector unchanged if the norm is zero.

nodes.name: qdrant.rs
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder file for a future Qdrant vector store adapter; currently contains no implementation.

nodes.name: lancedb_store.rs
nodes.summary: LanceDB-backed implementation of the Converge experience store contract that persists event envelopes alongside embedding vectors in an Apache Arrow column store and provides ANN-based vector similarity search.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges sync and async execution by holding a tokio Runtime and calling block_on for each public entry point; embedding vectors are stored as Arrow FixedSizeListArray columns with NaN/Inf validation enforced before writes.

nodes.name: LanceDbConfig

tour.title: Crate Entry Point
tour.description: lib.rs is the single public API surface of the manifold crate, declaring every adapter submodule with a `pub mod` entry per adapter family. Reading this file gives you an inventory of what Manifold owns: llm, search, fetch, feed, tools, storage, vector, experience, embedding, reranking — all behind feature flags. The fan-out of 24 direct imports makes it the highest-scope file in the codebase and the right place to start understanding how the pieces relate.
tour.languageLesson: Rust crates expose public items through their lib.rs root. Any submodule declared `pub mod` here becomes reachable as `manifold::module_name`. Feature flags (e.g., `#[cfg(feature = "llm")]`) let callers opt in to only the adapter families they need, keeping compile times and binary sizes small.

tour.title: Core Provider Contract Types
tour.description: contract.rs defines the shared vocabulary that every adapter in the crate speaks: the `Capability` enum classifying what a provider can do, `ProviderMeta` carrying provider identity, `ProviderCallContext` for per-call observation metadata, `TokenUsage` for cost tracking, and `CallTimer` for latency measurement. Every adapter family — from LLM to search to storage — depends on these types rather than defining its own, which is what makes providers interchangeable behind a single contract.

tour.title: Credential Resolution Chain
tour.description: With 19 fan-in edges, secret/mod.rs is the most widely depended-upon file in the codebase: every LLM adapter, every search adapter, and the model selector all call into it. It defines the `SecretProvider` trait and a layered `DefaultSecretProvider` that resolves API keys in order — macOS Keychain (keychain.rs, for developer machines), GCP Secret Manager (gcp.rs, for cloud deployments), then environment variables. names.rs provides the mapping from logical key names (such as `"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"`) to provider-specific aliases or GCP short names, so the same lookup works across all three backends without the caller caring which one is active.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's `zeroize` crate provides the `Zeroize` trait. `SecretString` wraps a `String` and calls `zeroize()` in its `Drop` impl, overwriting key material in memory when the value goes out of scope. This is the idiomatic Rust pattern for credentials: the type system enforces that secrets are cleared without relying on garbage collection timing.

tour.title: Model Registry & Selection Foundation
tour.description: Before any LLM call is made, Manifold needs to know which models exist and what each can do. config/models.yaml (2980 lines) is the canonical registry enumerating every supported model per provider with capability flags, context windows, and pricing. registry_loader.rs parses this YAML into typed `LoadedRegistry` and `LoadedModel` structs at startup, or falls back to an embedded default. model_selection.rs builds a `ModelSelector` from this data, encoding each model's capability matrix in `ModelMetadata`, and exposes a `ProviderRegistry` that gates candidate selection on whether a live credential actually exists for that provider.
tour.languageLesson: YAML is used for the model registry rather than Rust source because it lets operators extend or override the model list without recompiling the crate. The `serde` crate with `serde_yaml` deserializes the file into strongly-typed structs at runtime, catching schema mismatches early with clear error messages.

tour.title: Routing Intelligence
tour.description: Once candidate models are known, two modules work together to rank them. cost_routing.rs provides `CostBudget` — a filter that estimates per-call USD cost from token prices and rejects any model exceeding a configured ceiling, with a lenient mode for models whose pricing is unknown. fuzzy_fitness.rs implements a fuzzy-logic inference engine that scores each candidate on a dimensionless fitness value combining cost, latency, and quality inputs via membership functions and rules cached in `OnceLock`. The highest-scoring model that also passes the budget filter wins selection.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's `std::sync::OnceLock<T>` (stable since 1.70) is a thread-safe lazy initializer. fuzzy_fitness.rs uses it to construct the fuzzy membership functions exactly once on the first call and reuse them for every subsequent ranking, avoiding the overhead of rebuilding the inference engine per request in a concurrent async environment.

tour.title: LLM Adapter Dispatch
tour.description: llm/mod.rs (fan-out 20, fan-in 4) is the barrel that re-exports every LLM provider adapter as the subsystem's public surface. model_catalog.rs provides `ModelCatalog` — a cached, periodically-refreshed snapshot of OpenRouter's live model list — used to supplement the static YAML registry with fresh pricing and architecture metadata. llm/selection.rs is the factory that ties everything together: given a `ChatBackendSelectionConfig`, it queries the `ModelSelector`, verifies that a live secret exists for the chosen provider, and instantiates the right vendor-specific adapter struct, dispatching across all 14 supported providers.

tour.title: Representative LLM Adapters
tour.description: With the dispatch layer understood, it is time to see what an actual adapter looks like. anthropic.rs is instructive because Claude's native API diverges from OpenAI's schema — it uses typed content-part blocks, a separate system prompt field, and a distinct function-calling format, so the adapter must translate Converge's internal `ChatRequest` into this shape. openai.rs is the reference OpenAI-compatible implementation whose serialization pattern is reused verbatim by Arcee, Kimi, DeepSeek, MiniMax, Qwen, and four other thin adapters. openrouter.rs routes requests through a single aggregator endpoint and extracts per-provider cost from native usage fields. gemini.rs shows a third API shape: Google's content-part API with function calling.
tour.languageLesson: In Rust, trait objects (`Box<dyn ChatBackend>`) enable runtime polymorphism: each vendor adapter implements the same `ChatBackend` trait, so the rest of the system calls `backend.chat_async(request).await` without knowing which concrete type it holds. This is the mechanism that makes every provider genuinely interchangeable behind the same Converge contract.

tour.title: LLM Resilience Layer
tour.description: All 14 LLM adapters share a set of cross-cutting infrastructure modules that sit between the adapter and the caller. retry.rs provides the exponential-backoff loop with a typed `RetryOutcome` enum to distinguish retry-eligible transient errors from abort-worthy permanent ones. error_classification.rs maps vendor HTTP status codes into Converge-native error categories — auth failure, rate limit, model missing, parse error — giving the retry loop the signal it needs. format_contract.rs validates that responses conform to the requested output format (JSON, YAML, TOML) and annotates the response with the detected language via Unicode script heuristics. resilient.rs wraps any primary `ChatBackend` with an ordered fallback list, retrying on format failures or model-missing errors with alternative configurations. streaming.rs defines `StreamingChatBackend` and the `ChatEvent` enum for token-by-token output.

tour.title: Search & Fetch Adapters
tour.description: search.rs (fan-in 8, the second most-imported file in the codebase) defines the canonical search and fetch contract types: `WebSearchRequest`, `WebSearchResponse`, `WebFetchRequest`, `WebFetchResponse`, and the `WebSearchBackend` / `WebFetchBackend` traits that all vendor adapters implement. brave.rs provides `BraveSearchProvider` with capability tier support. tavily.rs provides `TavilySearchProvider` with AI-generated answer extraction. fetch.rs implements `HttpFetchProvider` — a hardened HTTP client that validates URLs against an SSRF blocklist, enforces redirect limits, and caps response body size. capability_registry.rs sits above these: it discovers available search, embedding, and reranking providers at runtime, scores them against declared capability requirements, and returns the best match.
tour.languageLesson: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) protection in fetch.rs rejects URLs that resolve to private IP ranges before any HTTP connection is opened. Rust's type system enforces this: URL validation returns a distinct `ValidatedUrl` newtype, making it a compile error to pass an unvalidated URL to the HTTP client — the protection cannot be accidentally bypassed.

tour.title: Object Storage Adapters
tour.description: object_storage/mod.rs exposes `build_store`, a URL-scheme-driven factory: a URI starting with `file://` routes to the local filesystem adapter, `s3://` to s3.rs, `gs://` to gcs.rs, and `hf://` to huggingface.rs. Every backend returns a value implementing the `object_store::ObjectStore` trait from the Apache Arrow ecosystem, so the rest of the application never needs to know which storage backend is active. The HuggingFace adapter is the most complex: it parses `username/dataset@revision` path segments, retrieves file metadata via HTTP HEAD against the Hub API, and downloads files through the `hf-hub` local cache rather than streaming directly.
tour.languageLesson: The `object_store::ObjectStore` trait (from the Apache Arrow / DataFusion ecosystem) defines a uniform async interface for `put`, `get`, `delete`, and `list` across S3, GCS, Azure Blob, and local storage. Manifold implements this trait for HuggingFace Hub, meaning any downstream tool that accepts a `dyn ObjectStore` can read HuggingFace datasets without any code changes.

tour.title: Vector Store Adapters
tour.description: vector/mod.rs exports `cosine_similarity` and `normalize` — the shared math utilities used by every vector store implementation. vector/lancedb.rs is the persistent backend: it serializes embedding vectors into Apache Arrow column format, manages Tokio runtime injection for tests, and provides full CRUD plus ANN nearest-neighbor search against LanceDB tables. vector/memory.rs is the lightweight alternative — a `RwLock<HashMap>` with brute-force cosine similarity search and optional minimum-score filtering, suitable for testing and small datasets. Both implement the same Converge vector store contract and can be swapped without changing application code.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's `RwLock<T>` allows many concurrent readers or one exclusive writer. vector/memory.rs uses `RwLock<HashMap>` because most vector store operations are reads (similarity queries) while upserts are infrequent, so `RwLock` provides better throughput than a `Mutex` for this read-heavy workload in an async Tokio context.

tour.title: Experience Stores & Multimodal ML
tour.description: The experience stores implement the Converge event persistence contract but target different query patterns. experience/lancedb_store.rs co-locates embedding vectors alongside event envelopes in an Apache Arrow column store and supports ANN-based vector similarity search — ideal for semantic retrieval of past experiences. experience/surrealdb_store.rs targets relational queries: artifact state-transition indexing, trace link traversal, and SurrealQL-powered event replay with full query expressiveness. Alongside these stores, embedding/qwen_vl.rs implements multimodal text and image embeddings via QwenVL (routing to HuggingFace, Alibaba DashScope, or a local HTTP service), and reranker/qwen_vl.rs uses the same three-endpoint routing pattern to rerank retrieved documents by relevance.

tour.title: Tools Subsystem & CI
tour.description: tools/definition.rs defines the core tool abstraction: `ToolDefinition` (the schema an LLM sees), `InputSchema` (JSON Schema for parameters), `ToolCall` (what the LLM requests), and `ToolResult` (what the handler returns with provenance). tools/registry.rs is the in-memory store with serialization helpers for both Anthropic format and generic OpenAI format, making the same tool list usable across providers. tools/openapi.rs converts any OpenAPI 3.x spec into `ToolDefinition` instances by mapping each HTTP operation to a tool with derived JSON Schema inputs — making any REST API instantly callable by an LLM. The CI pipeline (ci.yml) enforces these quality gates on every PR: cargo check, cargo test, clippy, and rustfmt against Rust 1.96.0. The crate Cargo.toml defines the feature flag matrix — one flag per adapter family — that keeps compile times lean for users who need only a subset.
tour.languageLesson: Cargo feature flags (`[features]` in Cargo.toml) enable conditional compilation with `#[cfg(feature = "llm")]`. Each adapter family is behind its own flag, so a product that only needs search compiles manifold without pulling in LLM or database dependencies. GitHub Actions CI runs `cargo check --all-features` to ensure every flag combination compiles cleanly.
